command:
set -eo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp LC_ALL=C
cd /tmp
echo "== verify the staged ChEMBL subset against its pinned sha256 =="
printf '%s  %s\n' 6fa986de4223948a169d954009a21cfe8a8286c1f9388c032c47f71af7993984 chembl37_first100k.tsv.gz > pins.sha256
sha256sum -c pins.sha256

echo "== Open Babel: the same 100,000 compounds RDKit did, via pybel =="
# NOT the obabel CLI. MEASURED on this image (Open Babel 3.2.1): `obabel -ismi x.smi
# -oinchikey` ABORTS at the first malformed SMILES and still exits 0 -- 5 molecules in with a
# bad one third gave 2 keys out, losing two VALID molecules after it; the same file with the
# bad record last gave 4. And `--append title` emits no identifier, so there is nothing to
# join on. Matching 100k results by row position would therefore have produced a confident
# wrong agreement rate that looked like the two toolkits disagreeing. pybel costs one row per
# bad molecule, catchably: 4 ok / 1 failed on both orderings.
T0=$(date +%s)
python3 - <<'PYEOF' > metrics.txt
import gzip
from openbabel import pybel, openbabel
openbabel.obErrorLog.SetOutputLevel(0)   # per-molecule parse errors are counted, not printed

rd = {}
for line in open("rdkit_keys.tsv"):
    p = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
    if len(p) >= 2 and p[1]:
        rd[p[0]] = p[1]

n = parsed = key_ok = skel_ok = both = rd_key = rd_skel = 0
out = open("ob_keys.tsv", "w")
with gzip.open("chembl37_first100k.tsv.gz", "rt") as fh:
    next(fh)
    for line in fh:
        cid, smi, std_inchi, std_key = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
        n += 1
        try:
            k = pybel.readstring("smi", smi).write("inchikey").strip()
        except Exception:
            k = ""
        out.write(f"{cid}\t{k}\n")
        if not k:
            continue
        parsed += 1
        if k == std_key:
            key_ok += 1
        if k.split("-")[0] == std_key.split("-")[0]:
            skel_ok += 1
        # The three-way: where BOTH toolkits produced a key, do they agree with each other?
        # InChI is canonical by construction, so two correct implementations must agree on a
        # molecule they both read the same way -- no tolerance to pick.
        if cid in rd:
            both += 1
            if k == rd[cid]:
                rd_key += 1
            if k.split("-")[0] == rd[cid].split("-")[0]:
                rd_skel += 1
out.close()
print("compounds %d" % n)
print("parsed %d" % parsed)
print("chembl_key_match %d" % key_ok)
print("chembl_skeleton_match %d" % skel_ok)
print("both_parsed %d" % both)
print("rdkit_key_match %d" % rd_key)
print("rdkit_skeleton_match %d" % rd_skel)
PYEOF
T1=$(date +%s); WALL=$(( T1 - T0 ))
cat metrics.txt
V(){ awk -v k="$1" '$1==k{print $2}' metrics.txt; }
N=$(V compounds); P=$(V parsed); CK=$(V chembl_key_match); CS=$(V chembl_skeleton_match)
B=$(V both_parsed); RK=$(V rdkit_key_match); RS=$(V rdkit_skeleton_match)
pct(){ awk -v a="$1" -v b="$2" 'BEGIN{printf "%.3f", 100*a/b}'; }
ROWS=$(awk 'END{print NR}' ob_keys.tsv)

{
  echo "compounds             $N   want exactly 100000"
  echo "keys_written          $ROWS   want == compounds   [one row out per row in]"
  echo "parsed_by_openbabel   $P   want exactly 100000 (RDKit managed 99997)"
  echo "chembl_key_match      $CK   ($(pct $CK $P)% of parsed)   want exactly 99846"
  echo "chembl_skeleton_match $CS   ($(pct $CS $P)%)   want exactly 99930  (RDKit: 99996)"
  echo "both_parsed           $B   (Open Babel and RDKit both produced a key)"
  echo "rdkit_key_match       $RK   ($(pct $RK $B)%)   want exactly 99926  [the neutral number]"
  echo "rdkit_skeleton_match  $RS   ($(pct $RS $B)%)   want exactly 99928"
  echo "wall_s                $WALL"
} > smoke-check.txt
cat smoke-check.txt
test "$N"  = '100000'
test "$ROWS" = "$N"
test "$P"  = '100000'
test "$CK" = '99846'
test "$CS" = '99930'
test "$B"  = '99997'
test "$RK" = '99926'
test "$RS" = '99928'
echo "SMOKE CHECK PASSED"
